title: Introduce credential-orchestrator and normalize stream payload framing across SDKs
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Teams reported duplicated credential logic and fragile stream payload framing across Python/TS/Go SDKs causing subtle reauth races and inconsistent user ergonomics (ENG-20142, ENG-20158). Motivation: provide a single orchestrator abstraction for credential lifecycle (warmup, lease, swap, fallback) and a small, consistent payload framing contract for streaming APIs so consumers don't need bespoke glue code. This PR implements a cross-language 'CredentialOrchestrator' pattern and a lightweight 'stream payload framing' contract, plus minor ergonomic surface tweaks and version bumps for parity. Key changes: - Introduce CredentialOrchestrator in each SDK: Python: redwood.session.CredentialOrchestrator (SessionWarmup + LeaseManager + fallback chain). TypeScript: CredOrchestrator with a single configure() entry and pluggable providers. Go: compact cred factory + orchestrator wrapper. - Stream payload framing: new minimal contract for chunk headers and resume tokens; SDKs expose helpers: build_payload_chunk(), parse_payload_chunk(), and an optional StreamPayloadAdapter that normalizes server-side variations. - Auth/retries: Centralize refresh scheduling, separate the refresh deadline from request timeouts, and add a deterministic backoff profile (default: jittered exponential with capped window) shared across SDKs. - Ergonomics: Python: introduce Session.handle_stream() coroutine helper; TS: stream() returns AsyncIterable<{kind, data}> with small discriminated union to avoid ad-hoc parsing; Go: added StreamReader helper that yields typed frames. - Parity and version bumps: python 1.12.0, typescript 2.4.1, go 1.7.3. Migration notes (short): - Python: replace Session.warmup + ad-hoc lease code with CredentialOrchestrator.start(session) and use session.handle_stream() to consume streaming responses. - TypeScript: pass a CredProvider to new CredOrchestrator.configure(); consumers can opt-in to StreamPayloadAdapter when connecting to older servers. - Go: use compactcred.NewOrchestrator(...) and StreamReader.ReadFrame() for streaming handlers. Testing & validation: - Unit tests added in each SDK for orchestrator handoffs and for payload framing edge cases (truncated chunk, resumed token mismatch). - Interop test harness run against staging streaming service (scenario matrix: reconnect, credential swap during active stream, long-lived lease expiration). - Load sanity run against the canary infra (no regressions observed in 99p latency, minor CPU uptick during warmup path). Backwards compatibility: - Default behavior maintains existing handshake semantics; StreamPayloadAdapter is opt-in for backwards compatibility. - CredentialOrchestrator is additive; existing simple credential providers continue to work. Decisions & tradeoffs: - We chose an orchestrator (single entrypoint) to reduce duplicated logic, accepting a small surface-area increase for SDK authors. - Kept payload framing intentionally minimal to avoid coupling to server wire format; server-side changes coordinated with API team. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-20142). - [x] Unit + integration tests. - [x] Interop run against staging. - [x] Docs snippets updated in SDK READMEs. - [x] Version bumps and changelog notes. Related: ENG-20142 design; SUP-7729 customer-facing support case describing stream reauth during long sessions.
commits: feat(sdk): add CredentialOrchestrator abstraction and adapters; feat(stream): add payload framing helpers and adapters; refactor(python): session warmup -> orchestrator; feat(ts): add CredOrchestrator configure+provider; feat(go): compact cred factory + orchestrator wrapper; test: add interop tests for resume/reauth; chore: bump sdk versions and changelogs

review_thread: Oliver Park (reviewer): We need clearer guarantees around orchestrator shutdown race with inflight requests. Maya: Added a shutdown() method and tests that assert inflight requests are allowed to finish while leases are swapped. Sofia Martinez (reviewer): TS API looks good but please avoid adding extra runtime allocations in the hot path. Maya: refactored adapter to reuse a shared buffer and added benchmark results to the PR description. Rajesh Patel (reviewer): Can we preserve older chunk formats? Maya: StreamPayloadAdapter is opt-in; added parsing fallback for legacy 'chunkv0' format. Oliver Park: CI flake on go test. Maya: reran CI and fixed a flaky test (timers), all green now.
release_notes: Introduce CredentialOrchestrator to centralize credential lifecycle and a small cross-SDK stream payload framing contract. Minor ergonomic helpers for consuming streaming responses. Version bumps: python v1.12.0, typescript v2.4.1, go v1.7.3.
